summary:
MARS 101: Your First Sols is a pixel-art mission trainer for kids aged 7 to 12. Players take the role of a junior astronaut running a small Mars habitat through their first four sols. They gather resources, craft supplies in a workshop with a monkey assistant, upgrade buildings, complete missions and repair breakdowns while managing energy, oxygen, water and food.

The challenge is addressed through real space-weather data. Solar events based on NASA's DONKI database (flares, coronal mass ejections, radiation storms) interrupt the mission, and the player must read the alert and decide how to protect the crew and equipment. Each landing zone has its own exposure to these events, so choosing where to settle changes the risk.

Kids learn that planning, resource management and space-weather awareness are part of real astronaut work, through play, with a built-in tutorial and manual. The game is fully bilingual (English and Spanish) and runs in the browser.

Created by students of ITZ, TecNM. It contains AI-generated art, code, text and audio, disclosed in the game's credits and in our documentation. Educational prototype, not an official NASA product.
details:
MARS 101: Your First Sols is an educational pixel-art survival game for kids aged 7 to 12, built as a "Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer". The player manages a small Mars habitat during the first four sols: gathering resources, crafting supplies in a workshop with the help of a monkey companion, upgrading buildings, completing main and side missions, and repairing breakdowns while keeping the colony's resources balanced.

How it works: the game schedules random solar events based on NASA's DONKI space-weather data (flares, coronal mass ejections and similar events). When one approaches, the player receives an alert and must decide how to protect the crew and equipment. Each landing zone on Mars has a different exposure to these events, so choosing where to settle changes the risk. Every run lasts four sols and a tutorial and in-game manual explain the rules.

Benefits and intended impact: kids learn, through play, that astronauts must plan, ration resources and watch space weather. The game is bilingual (English and Spanish) and runs directly in the browser, so teachers and families can use it without installing anything.

Tools: Godot 4 (GDScript), GL Compatibility renderer, exported to HTML5 and hosted on itch.io. Pixel art, UI and audio assets are included in the project. Data research used NASA's public DONKI information. We consider the following factors: age-appropriate difficulty, short sessions, clear alerts, and scientific accuracy at a simplified level.

Team: students of ITZ, TecNM (David Rosete Merino, Alexis Cruz Mazon, Enrique Jael Mendez Chanita). Mentor: M.C. Enrique Lopez Chavez.
